slides.headline: Nike lost $200 billion letting AI-detectable brand rot go unfixed for five years, these 6 prompts find the same rot in yours tonight.
slides.image_prompt: Nike swoosh — bold curved black checkmark — lying flat on a stainless steel medical examination table as a patient, an IV drip bag hanging above its curve, a pair of faceless hands pressing a chrome stethoscope to its center, a clipboard propped at the table edge bearing a large bold red downward-arrow line symbol. Stark white clinical examination room, harsh overhead fluorescent strip light. Documentary news photo, 35mm, on-camera flash, slight film grain. Zero readable text. Accent: signal red against clinical white.

slides.headline: 1) SPOT THE DISCOUNT TRAP BEFORE IT KILLS YOUR BRAND
slides.body: Nike trained customers to wait for sales, and by the time anyone noticed, full-price volume had collapsed. Then margins did too.
slides.image_prompt: A nearly bare athletic-shoe sale rack — metal pegs mostly empty, a few pairs remaining, bold red circular markdown-tag symbols dangling from each — while full-price display shelves stand untouched in the background. A silhouetted figure from behind walks directly toward the discount rack, bypassing the full-price wall entirely. Harsh fluorescent retail lighting. Documentary news photo, 35mm, on-camera flash, film grain. Zero readable text. Accent: signal red against retail grey.

slides.headline: 2) FIND WHO IS STEALING YOUR CUSTOMERS RIGHT NOW
slides.body: New Balance, Hoka, and On Running took four years of brand share from Nike before anyone inside noticed. Here is how to find who is doing it to yours:
slides.image_prompt: A bright retail shoe shelf holding three vivid competing sneakers in bold colors with one conspicuous empty slot at center. A pair of hands — no face visible — reaches toward the competitor shoes rather than the vacant gap. Tight close-up on the shelf, shoes sharp in focus. Clean white retail interior. Documentary news photo, 35mm, on-camera flash, film grain. Zero readable text. Accent: vivid orange against clean white.

slides.headline: 3) TEST IF YOUR ORIGINAL CUSTOMER HAS ALREADY LEFT
slides.body: Nike built its brand on serious athletes, then chased mass-market buyers. The core customer left, and the brand went with them.

slides.headline: 4) AUDIT YOUR BRAND STORY FOR COHERENCE
slides.body: Nike's slide accelerated when no one inside could answer 'why Nike and not Hoka?' The brand had drifted into generic over five years.

slides.headline: 5) WRITE YOUR CRISIS PLAN BEFORE YOU NEED ONE
slides.body: Nike had no fast response when the backlash grew. A gap like that takes weeks to close and costs far more than the 25 minutes this takes:

slides.headline: 6) PRICE YOUR PRODUCT LIKE YOUR BRAND DEPENDS ON IT
slides.body: Nike discounted its brand until its stock hit a 12-year low, down 78% from its all-time high. Each discount felt safe at the time.

slides.headline: SAVE THIS FOR TONIGHT
slides.body: Your brand is the most valuable thing your business owns. These 6 prompts take less than an hour. Nike took 5 years to fall.

caption:
Swipe through these 6 AI brand prompts, each one targeting a specific way a brand quietly dies before the numbers catch up. 🛡️

The discount trap that trains customers to wait for sales, finding who is stealing your customers right now, testing whether your original customer has already drifted away, auditing your brand story for coherence, writing a 24-hour crisis response plan, and pricing your product to match your brand's promise.

Nike's stock just hit its lowest level since 2014, down 78% from its all-time high, with over $200 billion in market cap gone. The collapse did not happen overnight. It happened through five years of quiet decisions that each felt safe at the time. AI lets any business owner run the same brand health check a consultant charges tens of thousands for, in one evening. Running a business? hook_tournament.why: [2] names Nike—a real, massive company—making me instantly curious what they supposedly missed, whereas [0]'s 'bleeding' metaphor stays abstract and requires me to click to even understand what the problem is. Specificity stops the scroll; vague drama doesn't.

editor_override: HOOK VIOLATION (§2): The hook is two hooks stapled with a comma — 'Nike lost $200 billion…' is one complete thought, 'these 6 prompts find the same rot in yours tonight' is a second separate actor and action. The doctrine requires ONE actor, ONE action; cut the weaker half and rebuild as a single clause. The Nike loss is the story; the prompts are the mechanism — one of them must anchor the hook.;
